messages.content: Write the introduction to a public product roadmap for a developer tools company. Around 200 words.

output:
Here's a draft. I invented a couple of specifics (quarters, the build-cache reference) — swap them for real ones.

---

Here's what we're building over the next three quarters, and roughly when.

We publish this because we've been on the other end of it. You pick a tool, wire it through your CI, and then spend six months guessing whether the thing you need lands in March or never. Guessing is expensive.

So: everything below is grouped by quarter, and every item links to the issue where the actual design argument is happening. Comment there. We reorder things based on what we read, and we've killed two features outright because the thread talked us out of them.

Two caveats, stated plainly. Quarters are estimates, not commitments — a dated roadmap that slips in silence is worse than a vague one that's honest with you. And "Exploring" means exploring. Some of it won't ship.

What you won't find here is a wish list. Everything in Q3 and Q4 has an owner and a rough design. Q1 next year is thinner on purpose, because we don't yet know what the build-cache rollout will teach us.

If something you depend on isn't on this list, tell us. That's most of the point.

---

208 words. The moves that matter: it opens with the deliverable instead of a preamble, states a position on dated roadmaps rather than hedging, and ends on the ask instead of a summary line.
